newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: LME zinc prices seen in technical correction - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc prices seen in technical correction - trade.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) three month zinc prices are likely to fall on technical factors later on Thursday after hitting a fresh 4-1/2 year peak of $1,279 a tonne on Wednesday, South Korean traders said.
"I expect the gap of between $1,254 and $1,262 made on yesterday's London market to be filled imminently," a futures broker in Seoul said. "It looks like a common gap."
But several traders said three-month zinc prices were expected to test a key resistance level of $1,300 a tonne before correcting.
The futures broker said the current zinc market was heavily overbought with the nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for three-month zinc standing at 74.98 percent.

He said the downward movement in zinc would be limited, due to fundamental support from high Japanese GSP zinc purchases ahead of the April 1 deadline for duty free imports, which are bolstering speculative interest in the metal.
"There is talk that the Japanese GSP zinc imports will be around 80,000 tonnes," he said.
Three-month zinc was indicated a touch easier at from London's close at $1,274 in Asian trend.
In general, traders said the current downtrend in copper prices would also help cap the rise in other metals.
One trader said three-month copper prices were expected to drift down to $2,280 a tonne unless Chinese buying emerges in the market.
Based on Elliot Wave theory, he said current copper levels looked like the end of the third wave and may fall to $2,180 a tonne.
The trader said, according to his foreign partners, there was still good consumer buying interest under $2,300 for three-month metal.
Three month copper was indicated slightly easier in Asian trade at $2,329/33 from London's close on Wednesday.
LME three-month aluminium was nearly unchanged in quiet Asian trade on Thursday from the previous day's London trade at $1,663/$1,668 a tonne.
